text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"stated position and repeated claim that cars are \"dangerous\" and \"unrealiable\"","quality":"clear stance","description":"It directly announces a position and keeps returning to that position throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"mentions lane changes, potholes, stop signs, and a child crossing the street","quality":"specific support","description":"It uses more concrete driving examples to show why a human driver may be safer."},{"evidence":"raises the issue of technology failing and quotes the article's liability question","quality":"use of source evidence","description":"It more clearly connects its argument to details and language from the article."},{"evidence":"develops the idea that drivers may become distracted or too comfortable","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"It shows a stronger sense of how driverless cars could create new risks through human behavior."},{"evidence":"separate opening, reasons in body paragraphs, and a closing question","quality":"basic organization","description":"It has a more recognizable argumentative structure with an introduction, body, and conclusion."}]}
